title: Temp-to-Perm Conversion and Evaluation Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This playbook defines Redwood Inference’s standard process for converting temporary (contract, contingent, or fixed-term) workers to full-time employees (FTEs). It covers eligibility, evaluation rubrics, manager and People Ops responsibilities, compliance checkpoints, and post-conversion onboarding adjustments. The goal is to create a fast, consistent, low-risk conversion path that preserves quality, legal compliance, and a positive candidate experience.

Scope:
- Applies to US and EU contingent workers engaged through Redwood’s vendors or directly contracted for 90+ days.
- Excludes interns (<12 weeks) and external contractors on project-only retainers unless agreed by VP People.

Definitions:
1) Contingent worker: contractor, agency temp, or fixed-term consultant.
2) Conversion candidate: contingent worker proposed for hire to an FTE role.
3) Hiring sponsor: manager proposing the conversion.

Key principles:
- Merit and role fit drive decisions; cost-savings are secondary to long-term role performance.
- Conversions must meet compliance (right-to-work, vendor contract terms, and local payroll rules) before offer.
- Managers should begin conversion conversations no later than 30 days before the anticipated conversion date.

Eligibility checklist (manager completes):
- Minimum tenure: 90 days on active assignment.
- Performance: 2 documented checkpoints with positive ratings or documented improvement plan completed.
- Role fit: position exists in headcount plan or business case approved by Finance.
- No active policy flags (IP, security, legal).

Evaluation rubric (qualitative + quantitative):
- Technical competency (35%): code quality, delivery velocity, peer reviews.
- Collaboration & communication (25%): cross-team work, feedback receptivity.
- Ownership & impact (25%): shipped work, customer-facing outcomes.
- Culture fit & coachability (15%): alignment with Redwood values and growth mindset.

Scoring guide (0-4 scale):
0 = insufficient data or performance below expectations
1 = inconsistent; needs coaching
2 = meets expectations
3 = exceeds expectations
4 = standout; ready for broader scope

Conversion timeline (recommended):
1) Day -45 to -30: Hiring sponsor flags intent in HRIS and notifies People Ops and Finance.
2) Day -30 to -20: Manager completes evaluation rubric and collects 2 peer references.
3) Day -20 to -12: People Ops runs compliance checks (vendor contract, eligibility to convert, payroll category).
4) Day -12 to -7: Compensation partner builds proposal; manager/People Ops confirm band/level.
5) Day -7 to 0: Offer approved by hiring committee (if external headcount) and extended to candidate.
6) Day 0: Candidate accepts and begins onboarding-to-perm adjustments.

Manager responsibilities (detailed):
- Initiate the conversion workflow in HRIS and attach rubric + peer notes.
- Provide two documented checkpoints (dates + topics) demonstrating performance.
- Coordinate interviews or calibration with hiring panel if role differs materially.
- Present business case to Finance when no existing headcount slot.

People Ops responsibilities:
- Verify vendor contract terms and any conversion fees.
- Coordinate background checks and right-to-work documentation.
- Prepare standard FTE offer template and benefits summary.
- If conversion requires external recruitment approval, schedule expedited hiring committee review (7 business days SLA).

Comp & Leveling guidance:
- Compensation should use the Redwood salary band that matches role level; managers may propose market adjustments with compensation approval.
- Consider continuity payments for loss of agency benefits where vendor requires settlement; People Ops handles vendor billing reconciliation.

Legal & Payroll checklist:
- Confirm termination of contingent agreement and start date for payroll.
- Ensure tax and social security onboarding steps per jurisdiction.
- Confirm any non-compete or IP assignment forms are executed.

Conversion offer steps (numbered):
1) Draft offer letter using /templates/converted-offer-template.docx.
2) Compensation signs off and stamps the offer with band details.
3) People Ops routes offer to candidate and sets a 5-business-day expiration.
4) Upon acceptance, People Ops triggers background checks and benefits enrollment.
5) Manager schedules a 1:1 to transition responsibilities and clarifies role expectations.

Onboarding adjustments after conversion (first 60 days):
- Day 1-7: HR check-in, benefits orientation, setup of permanent tools (email, laptop provisioning change if applicable).
- Week 2: Manager 30-minute calibration with People Ops to align success metrics and final role description.
- Week 4: Formal 1-month performance checkpoint documented in HRIS.
- Week 8: Career profile update and 90-day development plan drafted.

Performance & feedback cycle integration:
- Converted employees are folded into standard 6/12-month review cycles.
- Managers must document an initial development plan within 45 days of conversion.
- If conversion occurs mid-review cycle, the manager coordinates adjusted milestones with People Ops.

Metrics to track (People Ops):
- Conversion rate (%) by vendor and team.
- Time-to-offer from intent.
- Retention at 6 and 12 months post-conversion.
- Conversion NPS (candidate experience survey).

Template: Manager evaluation summary (copy-paste friendly):
"""
Candidate name: [Full name]
Role proposed: [Title]
Tenure on assignment: [days]
Rubric scores: Technical __/4, Collaboration __/4, Ownership __/4, Culture __/4
Narrative (200-400 words): [Manager summary of impact and recommendation]
Peer references (names & brief quotes):
Checkpoints (dates + topics):
Business case for hire (if required):
"""

FAQs (short):
Q: Can we convert sooner than 90 days?
A: Only in exceptional cases with VP People approval and vendor agreement.

Q: Who signs off on band exceptions?
A: Compensation Director.
